subject: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation (PaymentsInc)
messages:
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: bob.turner@paymentsinc.com, alice.chen@paymentsinc.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation (PaymentsInc)

Hi Bob / Alice —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment on pain, goals, and next steps. Please feel free to correct anything I missed.

Summary of pain points:
- Recent outages during peak batch settlement windows (2-3 incidents in last 6 months) causing delayed settlement and manual intervention.
- Inconsistent fallbacks between regions; traffic spikes have led to timeouts rather than graceful degradation.
- Lack of visibility into per-route token costs and KV cache hit rates; ops team is juggling cost vs latency trade-offs blind.

Current stack / constraints:
- Primary infra: managed Kubernetes on AWS (us-west-2) with vCPU-based autoscaling for model servers; running a mix of open LLMs (local fine-tuned) and an external vendor for high-priority flows.
- Data residency: payment data remains in their VPC, but redacted request metadata is permitted to be processed by a third party under a BAA.
- SLOs: 99.95% availability target for critical inference endpoints, 200ms p95 latency goal for synchronous calls.

Success criteria (what PaymentsInc needs from Redwood):
1) Predictable failover behavior: when a GPU pool or region degrades, traffic should automatically route to a compatible model variant with documented latency/cost trade-offs.
2) Observable degradation modes: clear metrics and alerts for fallback activations, KV cache miss surges, and per-route token cost spikes.
3) Auditability: retention of request/response metadata and audit logs for SOC2 compliance (30-90 day retention options discussed).

Incident history we discussed (from your notes today):
- 2026-05-12: us-west-2 autoscaler misconfiguration -> 45m outage for batch jobs
- 2026-08-03: model variant OOM under long-seq workload -> degraded responses; manual rollback performed
- 2026-10-11: cross-region routing delay during Cloud provider maintenance -> 12% error increase

Proposed Redwood approaches we covered:
- Smart routing policy: primary us-west-2, fallback to us-east-1 model variant (slightly larger quantized model) with circuit-breaker thresholds.
- Graceful degradation modes: soft timeouts returning condensed summary + error code instead of full failure; optional reroute to cheaper embedding-only fallback for non-critical requests.
- Autoscaling and reserved capacity: dedicated capacity for settlement pipelines during peak windows to hit p95 targets.
- Observability: per-route dashboards (latency, errors, cache hit rate) + rollout tracing and alerting tied to canary thresholds.

Next steps / action items:
- PaymentsInc: share incident logs and the SLO doc (you indicated an internal spreadsheet) -> I see you attached PaymentsInc_SLOs_and_incident_history.xlsx to the thread.
- Redwood (Ben): provide a tailored proposal including expected latency/cost for primary + fallback variants, recommended rollout plan, and a draft SLA for the dedicated settlement endpoints (ETA: Tue Nov 24).
- Technical deep-dive: schedule ~60m session with Rishi (serving/runtime) to walk through model variants, quantization options, and routing policies (target next week).
- Security: Marissa will follow up with the SOC2 / security evidence checklist and next steps for a BAA.

If that aligns, I’ll prepare the proposal and link a draft into the HubSpot deal and a shared Drive folder.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0156

Attachments: PaymentsInc_SLOs_and_incident_history.xlsx (spreadsheet), RFI_security_questions.pdf (PDF)
From: Bob Turner <bob.turner@paymentsinc.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: alice.chen@paymentsinc.com, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation (PaymentsInc)

Thanks Ben - this looks great and hits the key points. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) For the SLOs sheet, I attached the "official" internal SLOs in the XLSX you included; the most important is the 99.95% availability for settlement-critical calls (we measure rolling 30d).
2) We prefer cross-region fallback to us-east-1 only; ap-southeast fallbacks are out for now due to latency constraints for settlement windows.
3) For graceful degradation, our product team wants a non-blocking degraded response (summary + error code) rather than queuing for retries that could cause duplicate settlements.

Agree to the next steps. Please include an itemized cost delta for using dedicated capacity for the two 2-hour peak windows during settlement (US business days). Looking forward to the Rishi deep-dive - can we do Tues Nov 24 or Wed Nov 25 morning PT?

Appreciate it,
Bob Turner
Director, Platform Engineering
PaymentsInc
